why: A record with a registration number names the father (the 1984 form); the DNA measures the grandfather. X-009 asks for a record in hand; there are two kinds here.

decided: My prediction is reported as slightly missed.

decided: The owner's field-note instructions are relayed to the Demko agent in my note to it and in the Project copy.

decided: The owner's own match list is read for three numbers and no further.

decided: No match's family tree is opened and no match is contacted.
why: Rule 29 (no user-built online tree) and plain manners. The owner's override covers what he hands me, not what strangers posted.

decided: That the lists were made in 2026 is recorded and not objected to.

decided: The owner's three further match lists are read for the same three numbers as the first and no further.

decided: The pasted table is logged as a statement and a lead, with no document.

decided: The one-to-one comparison is put in the repository as text, with the two kit numbers cut to three characters.

decided: My own figure of B-063 is corrected in place, with the correction dated, and the site's figure is preferred.

decided: The report on the owner's own parents is recorded as a bare result.

decided: The grandfather's X list is described to the Demko agent, without names.

decided: The note on the DNA folder is written as field-notes/F-016-the-dna-folder.md.

decided: The three mitochondrial match lists are held and not used; one row count each.

decided: The Family Finder list is checked by program for surnames and villages of the two trees; rows outside the company's Paternal sorting are not read.

decided: A short note is written on the folder's reopening.

decided: The four files are logged as copies and not as the grandfather's.

decided: The grandfather's match list is read in full by program, and the ancestral-surname lists of the matches that bear on the trees are read; no match is named.

decided: H-100 is raised at 40.

decided: DNA leads are listed on the site and the DNA findings are carried onto the people they bear on and into a section of their own.

decided: Living matches stay unnamed on the site; a match's surname appears only where it is the lead.
